OPIOID TREATMENT PROGRAM - INITIAL INTAKE ASSESSMENT

Patient: 34-year-old male presenting voluntarily for admission to the opioid treatment program requesting maintenance therapy for opioid use disorder. Patient reports he has been using intravenous heroin daily for approximately 3 years, with escalating tolerance and unsuccessful attempts to quit on his own. He states he understands this is a chronic condition requiring ongoing treatment and is choosing to enroll in maintenance treatment of his own accord, having researched options and discussed with family.

Diagnosis: Meets DSM-5 criteria for opioid use disorder, severe, confirmed on interview - tolerance, withdrawal, unsuccessful efforts to cut down, continued use despite social/interpersonal problems, craving, and time spent obtaining/using the substance. Currently opioid-dependent, last use this morning per patient report, mild rhinorrhea and yawning noted on exam consistent with early withdrawal.

Medical history: No significant cardiac, pulmonary, or renal disease. Denies chronic pain conditions. Hepatitis C diagnosed 2 years ago, not currently treated. Denies pregnancy (male). No history of tuberculosis exposure reported. History of a motor vehicle accident 5 years ago with subsequent opioid prescription that preceded escalation to heroin use - reports lingering anxiety related to the accident.

Physical exam: Vitals stable, BP 128/82, HR 92, afebrile. Track marks noted bilateral antecubital fossae, healed. Mild diaphoresis, pupils normal size, no acute distress. Abdomen soft, nontender. No peripheral edema.

Labs: CBC, LFTs, TB screening (QuantiFERON), Hepatitis B/C panel, and HIV testing ordered today; hepatitis C confirmed positive from prior outside records reviewed and on file.

Informed consent: Reviewed methadone and buprenorphine treatment options in detail including risks (respiratory depression, QT prolongation, diversion risk) and benefits (reduction in illicit use, overdose risk, criminal activity). Patient signed informed consent form; expressed preference for methadone based on prior experience with buprenorphine causing precipitated withdrawal.

Treatment plan: Discussed availability of individual counseling, group therapy, and case management for housing/employment support. Patient interested in weekly individual counseling to start.

Withdrawal assessment: COWS score 8 (mild withdrawal). Plan for methadone induction starting at 30mg with reassessment in 2-4 hours per protocol, titration per program physician orders.

Safety assessment: Discussed overdose risk given reduced tolerance during induction period, warning signs of overdose reviewed with patient and his partner who accompanied him. Naloxone kit offered and dispensed today; patient and partner trained on use.

Care provided by program physician and licensed addiction counselor at certified OTP.

Plan: Begin methadone induction per above, follow up tomorrow for reassessment, drug testing per program protocol obtained today.
